candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12: safely administer medications, identify adverse effects/contraindications, monitor therapeutic response, and provide client education.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — HFrEF beta-blocker initiation during hospitalization
candidate.educational_objective: Initiate an evidence-based HFrEF beta-blocker after clinical stabilization, at a low dose, rather than during ongoing hemodynamic instability or IV inotropic support.

options.A: After the client is clinically stabilized and no longer requires IV inotropic support, with initiation before discharge when appropriate.
options.B: Immediately at a full target dose while marked low-output or hemodynamic instability persists.
options.C: Never, because evidence-based beta-blockers are contraindicated in every client with chronic HFrEF.
options.D: Only after all other guideline-directed HFrEF medications have first been permanently discontinued.

candidate.rationale: The 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA heart-failure guideline states that evidence-based beta-blockers should be used in HFrEF and can be safely initiated before hospital discharge provided the patient is clinically stabilized and does not require IV inotropic therapy for HF. It also advises caution with initiation after inotrope-requiring hospitalization and allows withholding or dose reduction when marked volume overload or marginal low output is present. A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Evidence-based beta-blockers in hospitalized HFrEF should be initiated after clinical stabilization, not during ongoing marked low-output instability or IV inotropic support, and can be started before discharge when appropriate.
candidate.source_document_title: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure
candidate.source_locator: §7.3.2 Beta Blockers: safe initiation before discharge if clinically stabilized and not requiring IV inotropic therapy; §9.2 Maintenance or Optimization of GDMT During Hospitalization: caution with initiation after inotropes; consider withholding/reduction with marked volume overload or marginal low cardiac output.
candidate.source_organization: American Heart Association / American College of Cardiology / Heart Failure Society of America
candidate.source_version_date: Published April 1, 2022; current guideline live-rechecked August 16, 2026
candidate.stem: A client hospitalized with acute decompensated HFrEF is being considered for initiation of an evidence-based beta-blocker. When is initiation most appropriate?
